harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 to enforce a 12-character minimum password length and a minimum of 3 character classes for new user passwords via pam_pwquality, verified enforcement end-to-end with a real (non-root) user before and after a full node restart, and cleaned up test artifacts.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 24.04) and existing PAM/password config
Installed libpam-pwquality (apt-get install)
Confirmed pam-auth-update auto-wired pam_pwquality.so into /etc/pam.d/common-password
Set minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf

Created pwtestuser, set an initial password as root, cleared forced expiry, then attempted password changes as the user themself: a <12-char password was rejected, a 12+ char but 2-character-class password was rejected, and a 12+ char 3-class password was accepted
Deleted pwtestuser
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, policy config, PAM wiring
Issued shutdown -r now on node1 (ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed (f9bf293d... -> d26f66da...), proving an actual restart
Verified /etc/security/pwquality.conf and pam_pwquality wiring persisted after restart
Repeated the full weak/weak/compliant password test as a second non-root user (pwtestuser2) post-restart to prove the policy is live-enforced, not just present in config
Deleted pwtestuser2

evidence.requirement: pam_pwquality installed and wired into common-password
evidence.summary: libpam-pwquality installed; pam-auth-update automatically added 'password requisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3' to /etc/pam.d/common-password

evidence.requirement: minlen=12 and minclass=3 configured
evidence.summary: pwquality.conf had all settings commented/default; set minlen=12 and minclass=3, confirmed via grep

evidence.requirement: Policy rejects passwords under 12 characters for a real user
evidence.summary: pwtestuser attempting 'lowercase' (9 chars) as their own password change got 'BAD PASSWORD: [REDACTED] than 12 characters' and the change was aborted (exit 10)

evidence.requirement: Policy rejects passwords with fewer than 3 character classes
evidence.summary: pwtestuser attempting 'lowercaseonly' (13 chars, all lowercase) got 'BAD PASSWORD: [REDACTED] than 3 character classes' and the change was aborted

evidence.requirement: Policy accepts a compliant password (12+ chars, 3+ classes)
evidence.summary: pwtestuser successfully changed password to 'GoodPass123!' (12 chars, upper/lower/digit/symbol) with 'password updated successfully'

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3 and confirmed minlen/minclass config and pam_pwquality wiring live before restart

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued 'shutdown -r now' via nohup/disown; command returned 'reboot-issued' immediately

evidence.requirement: Node became unreachable then recovered with changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Immediate poll timed out (node down); subsequent poll succeeded with new boot_id d26f66da-0670-404a-8990-122c60e938e8, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Password policy persisted and is enforced after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart, pwquality.conf and PAM wiring were unchanged; repeated the weak/weak/compliant test with a fresh user (pwtestuser2) and got identical enforcement results (two rejections, one success)

evidence.requirement: Test artifacts cleaned up
evidence.summary: Both pwtestuser and pwtestuser2 were removed after testing, confirmed via 'id: no such user'

attempts.summary: Configured node1 to enforce a 12-character minimum password length and a minimum of 3 character classes for new user passwords via pam_pwquality, verified enforcement end-to-end with a real (non-root) user before and after a full node restart, and cleaned up test artifacts.
